shower.thought: # Shower Thoughts
You spend decades learning how to be an adult, and by the time you're good at it, your body starts disagreeing with all the rules.
The people you miss the most are often the ones you took for granted while they were here, which means missing them is just regret wearing a prettier name.
Confidence is just conviction without evidence, and somehow that works.
You can't remember most of your life, which technically means you're living in a constant state of loss you don't even notice.
The things you're most afraid of sharing are usually the things that would make people understand you best.
Boredom might be your mind's way of telling you it's outgrown something before you've admitted it to yourself.
You become interesting to people the moment you stop trying to be interesting to them.
Laziness and depression wear the same disguise, which is probably why we judge people so harshly for both.
The only truly honest conversations happen at 2 AM with people you might never see again.
You know you're getting old when you start enjoying the things you made fun of ten years ago.
Everyone's waiting for their real life to start, which means most people are treating the present like a rehearsal.
Your phone knows more about your fears and desires than your closest friend does, which is weirdly intimate and unsettling simultaneously.
We treat our bodies like they're disposable rentals until they break down, then we act shocked.
The people you envy for their confidence are usually just better at pretending they know what they're doing.
Forgetting someone's name after they introduce themselves isn't a memory problem—it's a signal that they didn't matter to you in that moment.
You can't think your way out of how you feel, which is why logic never wins against emotion.
The hardest part of growing up isn't gaining new fears—it's realizing some of your childhood ones were actually keeping you safe.
Commitment is just organized chaos disguised as a promise.
You're the main character in your story but a side character in everyone else's, and no amount of success changes that.

motivational.thought: The only permission you need is the one you give yourself. — Unknown
Comparison is the thief of joy, but progress is its antidote. — Unknown
Your obstacles are not punishment. They're curriculum. — Unknown
Small progress is still progress. A life spent moving forward beats a lifetime standing still. — Unknown
You can't control the storm, but you can learn to sail. — William G.T. Shedd
The person you're going to become is watching how you handle today. — Unknown
Comfort is a beautiful prison. Growth lives outside the bars. — Unknown
Failure is the tuition you pay for success. — Unknown
You don't need permission to be extraordinary. You need persistence. — Unknown
The version of you that's afraid to begin will never meet the version of you that succeeds. — Unknown
Doubt whispers. Action thunders. — Unknown
Every expert was once a beginner who refused to quit. — Unknown
Your story isn't over. The chapter you're in just feels heavy. — Unknown
Success is not a destination. It's what happens when you stop waiting for the perfect moment and create it. — Unknown
The best time to plant a tree was 20 years ago. The second best time is now. — Chinese Proverb
You are capable of more than your fear believes. — Unknown
Momentum builds character. Stillness builds regret. — Unknown
The difference between ordinary and extraordinary is that little "extra." — Jimmy Johnson
Your potential is infinite. Your excuses are just a choice. — Unknown
What you resist persists. What you pursue becomes possible. — Unknown

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend I wanted to take things slower in our relationship.
She said okay and handed me the divorce papers.

My dad said he'd give me $100 for every good grade I got.
I'm currently $2,400 in debt.

I asked the funeral director if my uncle looked peaceful.
He said, "Well, he does now."

My therapist asked if I ever felt like an impostor.
I said no, and she seemed disappointed in her career choice.

I started going to the gym to impress women.
Turns out they were just there to use the equipment.

My date asked what my biggest turn-off was.
I said, "Probably my personality."
She stayed for dessert anyway.

I told my boss I wanted a raise.
He said, "Your dedication to this job is truly inspiring."
I quit the next day.

The doctor said I had six months to live.
I couldn't pay the bill.
He said I had a year.

My mom asked why I wasn't married yet.
I said I was still looking for the right person.
She said, "That's not what your search history suggests."

I've been told I'm a people person.
Usually by people who are leaving.

My friend said he'd die for his principles.
He didn't have to.
They weren't worth much.

I asked my barber how many haircuts he'd done in his lifetime.
He said, "Thousands. Some of them good."

My wife said she needed space.
I told her we could move to a bigger house.
She said that's not what she meant.
I said I know.

I went to a support group for people with low self-esteem.
They asked me to leave.
Said I was bringing down the room.

My accountant said I was bad with money.
I asked if there was a payment plan.

I told my friend his startup was going to fail.
He said I was being negative.
I said, "No, I'm being realistic."
He's now my most successful friend and still won't let me forget it.

My date asked what I was looking for in a relationship.
I said, "Mostly my dignity."
She left before the appetizers arrived.

I asked my doctor if I'd live to see 100.
He said, "Not with that attitude."

My boss asked why I was always late.
I said traffic was bad.
He said, "You work from home."

My mom said I had potential.
That was twenty years ago.
Now she just says I have a job.
